method: Direct review of six CatholicCulture-hosted DIRECTIONS reproducing Trapp (1955), Berger (1949) and Newland (1956); each described action anchored to line in hosted article. Not an original printed-book facsimile check; source-dependent recommendations not independent eyewitness attestations. Six further Newland hosted passages covered, including derivative Jesse-tree and home Tenebrae-inspired Stations; passage-level review does not verify original printed book or current prescribed indulgence. Final 17 hosted DIRECTIONS source articles (62 actions) read and source-actor, geographic range, ritual owner, testimony vs author adaptation scoped. 789 article has a source author attribution discrepancy. These are readings of hosted excerpts, not scans of original books.

source_groups.author: Maria Augusta Trapp
source_groups.book_source: Around the Year with the Trapp Family (1955)
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Explicit eyewitness account of the Trapp family's Christmas Eve ceremony, with occasional wider claims; no universal ritual ownership inferred.

source_groups.author: Florence Berger
source_groups.book_source: Cooking for Christ (1949; reproduced edition 1999)
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Mix of Berger family's Wisconsin reminiscence, parish blessing at High Mass, forgotten local custom in another parish, folk beliefs and author's household dishes; neither blessing nor superstitious efficacy universalized.

source_groups.author: Florence Berger
source_groups.book_source: Cooking for Christ (1949; reproduced edition 1999)
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Berger reports Sicilian St Joseph table and poor beneficiaries; explicitly says her family did not stage so large an observance. Recipes are narrower author suggestions, not evidence of separate Catholic customs.

source_groups.author: Mary Reed Newland
source_groups.book_source: The Year and Our Children (1956)
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Domestic Advent wreath: multiple construction, candle, prayer, teaching and family lighting variations described as practice or advice by one author, attached to already-published Advent wreath identity; no separate new customs.

source_groups.author: Mary Reed Newland
source_groups.book_source: The Year and Our Children (1956)
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Newland suggests a private home vigil with texts reused from church liturgy and explicitly states some blessings are out of context; reserve church rite and lay devotional adaptation in separate lanes. No claim of authorized priestly blessing by lay leader.

source_groups.author: Mary Reed Newland
source_groups.book_source: The Year and Our Children (1956)
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Domestic family Rogation walk and Litany personally adapted; priestly leading/blessing remains ministerial; French Canadian grains and monastery procession are distinct reported regional or institutional practices.

source_groups.book_source: Cooking for Christ (1949, hosted excerpt)

source_groups.book_source: Cooking for Christ (1949, hosted excerpt)
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Historical narrative about Greek and Latin fasting on Exaltation must not be asserted as a currently binding universal fast; fairs are largely secular harvest markets; Luke patronage a separate example.

source_groups.book_source: The Year and Our Children (1956, hosted excerpt)

source_groups.book_source: The Year and Our Children (1956, hosted excerpt)
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: St Barbara family dinner is not Barbarazweige branches. Newland explicitly flags questionable Acts, so hagiographic details not automatically accepted as history; collect recited domestically is prayer, not lay Mass celebration.

source_groups.book_source: The Year and Our Children (1956, hosted excerpt)
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: One family's devotional gift-crafting and conversation illustrated by Immaculate Conception, not independent liturgical rite or certified historic custom.

source_groups.book_source: The Year and Our Children (1956, hosted excerpt)
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Gourd typology is author's catechetical Easter-egg symbolism; the biblical typology itself is not evidence for a historically established gourd-egg regional custom. Exact symbol at printed line 170.

source_groups.book_source: The Year and Our Children (1956 excerpt; CatholicCulture hosting includes later site framing)
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Newland explicitly borrows Berger cake icing and the French king bean/pea; her extra tokens have invented symbolism. Hosted article also includes priestly Epiphany chalk/home blessings and lay prayer variants beyond these five particular source action rows—these are separate ritual-authority issues, not proof the author validated a lay Roman Ritual priest formula.
